scams.sectionSubtitle: Recognize the most prevalent fraud schemes currently targeting citizens in India
scams.upiDesc: Scammers promise refunds or rewards and send a UPI collect request. Entering your UPI PIN always sends money; receiving money NEVER requires a PIN.
scams.upiRule: Golden Rule: UPI PIN is ONLY entered to deduct money, NEVER to receive money.
scams.digitalArrestTitle: Digital Arrest / Fake Police Video Call
scams.digitalArrestDesc: Fraudsters pose as CBI, ED, Police, or Customs officers claiming your Aadhaar or mobile SIM is linked to money laundering or illegal parcels. They demand video confinement and money transfer.
scams.digitalArrestRule: Law enforcement never conducts trials, arrests, or money demands via Skype, WhatsApp, or video calls. Hang up immediately and dial 1930.
scams.electricitySmsDesc: SMS threats stating your power will be disconnected tonight due to unpaid bills, prompting you to call a fake officer or install a remote-access app (AnyDesk/QuickShare).
scams.electricitySmsRule: Electricity distribution companies never send SMS asking you to call personal mobile numbers or download APKs.
scams.partTimeJobDesc: Earn quick money by liking YouTube videos or rating hotels, followed by demands to deposit money into crypto or fake investment wallets.
scams.partTimeJobRule: Any job that requires you to pay money to earn money or unlock withdrawals is 100% fraudulent.
scams.quishingDesc: Malicious QR stickers pasted over parking meters, restaurant tables, or petrol pumps directing you to cloned credential-stealing portals.
scams.quishingRule: Never scan unknown QR codes to receive payments, and always inspect the destination URL before entering credentials.
